material_changes.title: Persistent agent memory can launder authorization state
verified_facts: arXiv:2609.01836 was submitted on September 1, 2026 and is categorized under cs.CR and cs.AI.
The paper defines endogenous authorization laundering as false permissions entering persistent agent memory and later being treated as valid authority.
The authors evaluate five LLMs as memory writers and two as executors across procurement, cybersecurity and finance.

The paper reports false authority for up to 50.2% of unauthorized requests under incremental memory updates and executor action on false authority in 98.6% of trials once the false authority is present.
The paper reports that source-event-backed permissions and bounded event sourcing reduce the problem while introducing a safety-utility tradeoff.
missing_verification: Inspect the full benchmark design, prompts, models and statistical methodology.
Verify whether code, benchmark data or evaluation artifacts are publicly available under a usable license.
Reproduce a small benign authorization-state fixture before adapting any repository control.
Compare the proposal against existing repository provenance, integration-queue and current-repo-truth contracts to avoid duplicating policy without enforcement.
material_changes.recommended_action: Integrity/Build should evaluate source-event-backed authorization and bounded event-sourcing concepts on benign local agent fixtures. Adopt no enforcement or security claim until the benchmark and implementation artifacts are independently reviewed.
